CONTRACT (the doc; follow it exactly)
Turns a title into a slug for file names: lowercase ASCII words (letters a–z and digits 0–9) joined by single underscores. Letters outside a–z are converted to their usual ASCII spelling rather than dropped: accents are removed (é → e, ü → u) and special letters are spelled out (ß → ss). Every run of other characters (spaces, punctuation, symbols, hyphens and existing underscores) becomes a single underscore, and the slug never starts or ends with an underscore. A title without any letters or digits gives the empty string.

- "removes accents"
- "spells out special letters in German, Nordic and Polish words"
- "collapses runs of spaces and punctuation into one underscore"
- "trims separators from both ends"
- "keeps digits"
- "turns hyphens into underscores without doubling them"
- "gives an empty string when there is nothing to keep"
Properties (fast-check generates many inputs, including edge cases):
- "output is lowercase letters and digits joined by single underscores"
- "slugifying a slug changes nothing"

FINAL REMINDER
- Do not run any shell command, do not read or inspect any file, do not use any tool.
- Reply now with ONLY the JSON object {"body": string, "notes": string}; "body" holds only the statements between the braces.
